A small Samoyedic people of the lower Yenisei River in Arctic Siberia, shown on the map in 1530 and 1600 near the river's mouth. They herded and hunted reindeer, fished and trapped, moving with the seasons across the tundra and the edge of the forest.

Their nearest kin are the Nenets to the west and the Nganasan to the east, all speakers of Samoyedic languages. Russian fur traders reached the Yenisei in the early 17th century, during the Russian conquest of Siberia, and the Enets had to pay tribute in furs. Today only a few hundred remain.
